title: A password signs a device in to jellyscale's own API
description: Serves "Joining and signing in are easy and safe.".
acceptanceCriteria: A password gives a device its own sign-in, which signing out ends.

A wrong password, an unknown name and a disabled account given a wrong password get the same answer, in the same time. Tries are bounded per name, with the bounds built today, and a name that does not exist is bounded the same way.

A refused sign-in carries a reason Octave can explain: name or password not accepted (retry), try later (with how long), or, only after the right password on a disabled account, ask the operator. No answer tells a viewer which names exist.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.
The sign-in answer names the account, the profile and the device, each with its own id.
No sign-in credential is stored in the clear: one read from the database signs no one in, shown by trying one.
